entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Vital du Four (c. 1260 – 1327) was a pivotal French Franciscan theologian and scholastic philosopher whose intellectual contributions significantly influenced late medieval thought and ecclesiastical politics during the tumultuous Avignon Papacy. Elevated to cardinal in 1312 by Pope Clement V, his career bridged profound academic inquiry with high-stakes curial service, making him a central figure in the intellectual and political currents of early 14th-century Western Europe. His work is notable for its rigorous defense of Franciscan ideals and its engagement with the burgeoning philosophical debates of the era, particularly concerning logic and metaphysics.

Born around 1260, Vital du Four joined the Franciscan Order, rapidly ascending through its academic ranks. He taught at the University of Montpellier and the University of Paris, where he earned his doctorate in theology by 1307. His major works include the *Speculum morale*, a vast compendium of ethical and theological thought, and his *Quodlibeta*, which addressed a wide array of philosophical and theological questions debated in the Parisian schools. He participated in the Council of Vienne (1311-1312), where he played a role in the discussions concerning the Knights Templar and the Spiritual Franciscans. Pope Clement V appointed him Cardinal-Priest of Santi Silvestro e Martino ai Monti in December 1312, and later Cardinal-Bishop of Albano in 1321.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Vital du Four was a prominent Franciscan cardinal and theologian whose scholastic writings significantly influenced theological debates on the Immaculate Conception and Aristotelian thought. His curial involvement provided a crucial voice in papal politics during the Avignon Papacy.
